subject: Physics
description: Work, kinetic energy, conservation of momentum, simple machines

questions.stem: The KINETIC ENERGY of a body of mass m moving with velocity v is:
questions.explanation: KE = (1/2)mv². Unit: joule. mv is momentum. If v doubles, KE × 4. If m doubles, KE × 2. Work-energy theorem: net work = change in KE.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The principle of CONSERVATION OF MOMENTUM states:

options.option_text: In a closed system (no external force), total momentum remains constant
Every action has an equal and opposite momentum

questions.explanation: Conservation of linear momentum — follows from Newton's 3rd law applied to pairs of interacting bodies. Collisions: total momentum before = total after. Rocket propulsion works on this principle (exhaust ejected backward → rocket moves forward).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The SI unit of WORK is:
questions.explanation: Work done = Force × displacement × cos θ. 1 Joule = 1 Newton × 1 metre. Also 1 J = 1 kg⋅m²/s². 1 calorie ≈ 4.184 J. Newton — force. Watt — power (J/s).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: A simple PENDULUM has maximum KINETIC energy at:
questions.explanation: Pendulum: at extreme positions, velocity = 0 → KE = 0, PE = max. At mean position (lowest), velocity = max → KE = max, PE = min (zero if taken as reference). Total energy is conserved. Time period T = 2π√(L/g).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: A force of 10 N moves an object through a distance of 5 m in the direction of the force. The work done is:
questions.explanation: W = F·d·cos(θ) = 10·5·cos(0°) = 50 J. If force is perpendicular to motion, θ = 90°, cos(90°) = 0 → W = 0 (e.g., gravity on a horizontal sliding object).
questions.subject: Physics

options.option_text: Rate of doing work (or rate of energy transfer)

questions.explanation: P = W/t (work done per unit time). SI unit: Watt (W) = J/s. Also P = F·v for constant force. 1 HP ≈ 746 W. Electrical power: P = VI = I²R = V²/R.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: Which is NOT a simple machine?
questions.explanation: Six classical simple machines: lever, wheel & axle, pulley, inclined plane, wedge, screw. An electric motor is a COMPOUND machine that converts electrical → mechanical energy.
